title: Trace how a web-scale candidate becomes a governed manifest
description: Choose an operating condition. Active routes show where immutable evidence, quarantine, versioning, and removal propagation change the outcome.

nodes.label: Candidate index
nodes.detail: Stores discovery metadata and crawl identity. A URL is a locator, not immutable image content or permission.

nodes.label: Fetch quarantine
nodes.detail: Downloads into a bounded sandbox, validates media type and size, and prevents malformed or changed content from entering trusted shards.

nodes.label: Decode and fingerprint
nodes.detail: Normalizes media, records cryptographic and perceptual hashes, detects duplicates, and binds later scores to exact bytes.

nodes.label: Versioned score bank
nodes.detail: Stores raw signals with model, preprocessing, threshold, and calibration versions instead of one composite quality number.

nodes.label: Release manifest
nodes.detail: Names every included candidate, content hash, source context, score versions, filter reasons, review state, and shard assignment.

nodes.label: Immutable shards
nodes.detail: Materializes approved pairs for one release. New scores or removals create a new manifest and shard lineage.

nodes.label: Audit and removal registry
nodes.detail: Records restricted hashes and URLs, reviewer evidence, appeals, downstream manifests, and required removal propagation.

nodes.label: Slice evaluation
nodes.detail: Compares modalities, languages, sources, policy errors, and downstream model behavior before approving a release.

scenarios.label: Build a release
scenarios.summary: Candidate metadata is fetched into quarantine, bound to exact bytes, scored with versioned models, evaluated by slice, and materialized from an approved manifest.
scenarios.result: A release can be reproduced because every included pair, score version, decision reason, and shard derives from one immutable manifest.

scenarios.label: URL content changed
scenarios.summary: A previously indexed URL now serves different bytes. Reusing old scores would attach evidence to the wrong media.
scenarios.result: Treat the new hash as a new candidate, rescore it, and preserve the old hash-to-manifest lineage instead of silently replacing content.

scenarios.label: Restricted hash match
scenarios.summary: The audit registry identifies a restricted URL or image hash before release materialization.
scenarios.result: Block and quarantine the candidate without exposing prohibited content to general review queues; record the minimum evidence and follow the escalation policy.

scenarios.label: Scorer version changed
scenarios.summary: A new aesthetic or alignment model changes scores and slice retention. Overwriting old columns would make previous releases irreproducible.
scenarios.result: Write a new versioned score column, compare decision changes by slice, recalibrate thresholds, and publish a new manifest only after review.

scenarios.label: Removal request
scenarios.summary: A reviewed request or incident affects content already referenced by one or more released manifests and shards.
scenarios.result: Trace every affected manifest, publish successor manifests and shards, document downstream propagation, and prevent the restricted identity from re-entering on a later crawl.
